senses.definition: A cycle where each turn feeds the next, so growth gets easier the longer it runs.
senses.caution: It claims a specific mechanism, so you should be able to say each step of the loop out loud before you use it - in an investment room someone will ask you to draw it, and growth that is merely fast has no loop in it at all. It also carries a built-in excuse for a flat early stretch, which is a very convenient thing to reach for when your numbers are flat. Bezos put the word in every strategy deck for a decade, so in some rooms it arrives pre-discounted as consultant language.
senses.example: Every deployment hands us the failure cases the next model trains on. That's the flywheel, and honestly it's the only moat we have.

cues.text: You are explaining to an investor why the product improves the more it is used, and you want a single term for that loop instead of three sentences of mechanism.
A sponsor asks why usage sat flat for two quarters and then bent sharply upward, and you want the term for growth that starts slowly and then compounds.
In a strategy session someone claims the product has a moat. You want the word for the loop they would have to be able to draw for that claim to survive the next question.
A bakery near you got busy because the queue outside made passers-by curious, and the queue got longer, and you want a word for what happened to it.

distractors: A rig that drives a system to see how it behaves under conditions you choose.
Progress won into territory that was previously closed to you.
A people scattered from a homeland who keep a tie to it.
A structure where everyone can be watched at any moment and nobody knows when they are.
The unwritten history an organisation holds about why its own systems were built that way.
